subject: Choosing the billing lane: marketplace listing timelines vs direct PO for enterprise procurement
messages:
From: Emily Clarke <emily.clarke@finwellhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11 09:12 -0700
Subject: Question on fastest path to buy (AWS listing vs direct PO)

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team is excited about Redwood for our customer-facing agents. Procurement at FinWell wants to confirm timelines and trade-offs before we commit a PO. Two specific asks: 1) If we go through AWS Marketplace (public listing / private offer), how long before we can get an invoice and start billing? 2) If we do a direct contract with Redwood (purchase order + invoice), what are typical lead times and any gating items on your side (SOC2 addendum, finance onboarding)?

We also attached our standard PO template and would appreciate any redlines up front. Short on time — can you point me to the fastest path to get a July start?

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Clarke
VP, Procurement — FinWell Health
Attachments: FinWell_PO_Template.pdf

Looping you both in — FinWell wants to understand marketplace vs direct PO timing and any compliance gating (SOC2 addendum, invoice SOW cadence). Quick thoughts below; Ben, can you confirm marketplace lead time and private-offer process? Laura, any finance onboarding notes we should flag (tax forms, W9, wire instructions)?

Proposed quick answer to Emily: Marketplace private offer is typically fastest to sign and bill if they accept marketplace terms (private offer processing + AWS approval) — can often be done in 1–2 weeks for standard SLAs. Direct PO + invoice can take 2–4 weeks depending on legal review and finance onboarding, but gives more flexible commercial terms (po-term edits, billing address etc.).

I attached the PO they sent. Ben — can you review and advise on any required changes to make that path faster?

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-11 13:25 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Question on fastest path to buy (AWS listing vs direct PO)

Thanks for the heads up, Olga. Quick practical notes (marketplace vs direct):

- AWS Marketplace (private offer):
  * Time to invoice: once the private offer is accepted and AWS processes it we can get billing live typically within 3–10 business days. If they already have AWS procurement workflows it can be on the shorter side.
  * Benefits: speed, buyer familiar with marketplace purchases, easier to consume credits/commitments, AWS-managed billing helps their FinOps.
  * Trade-offs: pricing flexibility is constrained vs a negotiated direct PO; revenue recognition flows through AWS which can affect co-sell crediting timing.

- Direct PO / Redwood invoice:
  * Time to invoice: depends on legal & finance gating — typical range 7–21 business days. If they require custom T&Cs we need Legal review which adds time.
  * Benefits: more flexible payment terms, direct MSA amendments, easier to include custom indemnities or audit clauses.
  * Trade-offs: procurement often requires W-9, completed tax forms, and sometimes an EFT/wire setup — ask them for preferred payment method to pre-seed finance paperwork.

Compliance gating: SOC2 addendum — we can provide our standard SOC2 attestation and a short addendum; Legal turnaround is usually 3–5 business days for standard language. If they require an on-site audit or extra clauses, that will add time.

Suggested next steps for speed:
1) If FinWell accepts standard marketplace/private-offer terms, route via AWS private offer and request acceptance asap. We'll prepare a private-offer draft and the AWS listing team will intake it.
2) If they require custom commercial terms, have procurement return a marked-up PO and list must-have contract terms up front so Legal can triage quickly.
3) Ask FinWell to confirm billing preference (AWS invoice vs Redwood invoice) and payment method — we can pre-create finance onboarding docs.

I can draft the private offer text and attach Redwood terms if helpful.

Ben Carter
Senior Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Emily Clarke <emily.clarke@finwellhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12 09:04 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on fastest path to buy (AWS listing vs direct PO)

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement here prefers to move fastest: they can accept a marketplace private offer if Redwood can issue the private offer draft today and we can get the acceptance routed in parallel. That will let us move forward without a lengthy legal review.

A couple of clarifying items from our side: 1) We need to know whether AWS billing would show Redwood as the vendor (for our internal chargebacks). 2) If marketplace, will the PO still be valid to attach for our internal controls or do we need to use AWS invoice only?

I'll approve the AWS private offer route provided Redwood confirms timelines and provides the private-offer draft and the SOC2 attestation.

Emily
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Emily Clarke <emily.clarke@finwellhealth.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12 16:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on fastest path to buy (AWS listing vs direct PO)

Hi Emily — copied team from Finance. Short answers:

1) AWS billing: invoices are issued by AWS Marketplace and will reference the product as sold via AWS; the invoice line item indicates the vendor is Redwood. Many customers use that invoice for internal chargeback — you can attach FinWell's PO as a supporting doc in your systems.

2) PO validity: You can still keep your Purchase Order; FinWell often attaches the PO to the AWS invoice for internal controls. If FinWell needs Redwood to issue a separate invoice under direct contract we can do that but it delays start time.

Next steps we will execute now:
- Ben will share the private-offer draft and Redwood terms (we'll include SOC2 attestation).
- Emily: confirm the AWS account/marketplace contact (email or AWS account id) so we can submit the private offer.
- If procurement still wants Redwood invoice instead of AWS, let us know ASAP — we'll kick finance onboarding but that will push the earliest start date by ~2 weeks.

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Finance Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_PrivateOffer_Terms_v2.pdf
